reproduced_defect: A persisted tool-call can name an account that is no longer present after restart. Blindly recreating ForegroundAccountReservations for that stale id can consume the apparent reservation capacity of a one-account pool for unrelated work even though the configured replacement account is actually free.
exact_source_basis: ForegroundAccountReservations.reserve accepts an arbitrary account_id and wait_for_turn_route compares distinct reserved ids with pool_size.
NotionAccountPool.status returns the current configured account ids in accounts[].id, so Core can validate a persisted owner without probing Notion or mutating pool policy.
Current durable-replay product code is not yet integrated; this is an ordering/rehydration guard for the pending V8/V9/V10 patch.
required_v11_rule: Before rehydrating a persisted tool-call reservation, obtain the current configured account-id set from the already-constructed local account pool.
If persisted account_id is still configured, reserve exactly that account before any identity-bearing replay is sent to Codex.
If persisted account_id is absent, clear any stale in-memory reservation and fail closed; do not silently substitute another account/thread in Core.
A later NOTION_AGENT integration may provide an explicitly proven full-history rebase/failover path; Core must not invent one.
